name: Lyo.Health
tagline: Interface for services that report their own health. Implement `IHealth`. There is no central health service.
description:
Interface for services that report their own health. Implement `IHealth`. There is no central health service. Health returns `HealthResult` with status,
timings, and optional metadata.

HealthResult.Unhealthy(sw.Elapsed, "Database connection failed", metadata: null, exception: ex);

sections.title: Contract
sections.body:
- `HealthCheckName` is a short identifier used to label probe output in hosts, for example `"filestorage"`, `"cache"`, `"rabbitmq"`, `"audit-postgres"`, `"change-tracker-postgres"`.
- `CheckHealthAsync` is the live probe. Keep it cheap and short-circuiting, and honor the supplied `CancellationToken`.

sections.title: `HealthResult`
rows: How long the probe took (typically measured with `Stopwatch`).
UTC instant the probe completed (set by the factory helpers).
Optional human-readable summary; populated with the exception message on failure.
Connection info, schema, version, key-id, etc.
Captured exception when the probe threw.
sections.lead: `HealthResult` is an immutable, sealed class for the outcome of a probe:
sections.trail: Use the static factories rather than constructing directly:

sections.title: Usage
sections.text: Get health from the service directly. Service interfaces (`IFileStorageService`, `ICacheService`, `IMqService`) extend `IHealth`. Health comes from the service. No separate registration. Hosts that need an aggregate view typically resolve `IEnumerable<IHealth>` and fan out `CheckHealthAsync` in parallel, then publish the resulting `HealthResult` collection.
